Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's all we have from this game. We look forward to your company on 25th March for the fourth Test match in Dharamsala. Do join us at 0930 local (0400 GMT) for all the action. Cheers!!

Man of the Match, Cheteshwar Pujara says his innings was much needed for the team. Feels that there was a position where they lost six wickets (on day 3) and he talked to Saha about having a partnership. Admits he was aware that he needed to bat long. When asked about his patience, he states that he also gets tempted to play big shots but he looks at the bigger picture. Opines that India couldn't effort to lose a wicket at that time and so he looked to rotate the strike. Adds that this is how he avoids to go over the top or play the sweep shot. Says that he doesn't need any motivation while playing for India. States that they are the number one team and look to play like that. Further adds that to put the opposition under pressure at lunch with four wickets down they thought they had the game but also adds that Shaun Marsh and Peter Handscomb batted really well. On fitness and fatigue, he replies that batting long affects his fitness but he has been working hard and concentrating on diet. Ends by saying that he hopes to recover for the Dharamsala Test in time.

Virat Kohli says that they were in a good position after losing the toss. Also says KL Rahul and Murali Vijay were outstanding and Pujara's knock was unbelievable. Praises the partnership between Saha and Pujara which allowed them to get into the lead. Adds that after getting two wickets yesterday they really thought they had a chance. Credits Peter Handscomb and Shaun Marsh for their brilliant batting. Also praises his boys for showing great mental strength. On Pujara's knock, Kohli replies that he is someone who takes a lot of pride in his performance, knows his game really well and is a hardworking batsman. Adds that to him it was his best knock. On Wriddhiman Saha's innings, Kohli says that he did it in West Indies and against New Zealand in Kolkata and once again really stood up and did the job. Opines that the wicket was not offering much and the old ball was not gripping. When asked about Jadeja's effort in the match, Kohli replies that he is gun in the field and has never seen someone so economical. Signs off by saying that they are looking forward to the next game.

Steven Smith says it was a nervous final day and feels it was a brilliant Test match. Adds that it's all about showing resilience and standing up in tough situations. He praises Shaun Marsh and Peter Handscomb for digging in deep and earning a draw. Also adds that they batted beautifully and it was very crucial for the team. On his knock, Smith replies that it was a nice wicket and first innings runs were vital. Quickly adds that 450 was not enough to win this game and credits India for batting beautifully. He also has a word of praise for Glenn Maxwell and says that he was sensational and that's the way they want him to bat. Also praises Pat Cummins for his effort on this pitch. He is really proud of the way his boys played and is looking forward to Dharamsala.

On the last day when all predictions were about India, as to how fast they could wrap up this game, the visitors stepped up their game. Marsh and Handscomb showed grit and determination to do what they did. Ravichandran Ashwin only took two wickets and was far from his best. However, Ravindra Jadeja bowled his heart out and was always at the batsmen. But either team would be content with the result as both of them were behind at some point of time. Now the attention shifts to the fourth Test. But before that, lets see what the captains and the Man of the Match say at the presentation...

It was a tricky phase for India in the last session of day 3 as they lost Karun Nair and Ravichandran Ashwin quickly. But then came the knock of the series! Time and again, Cheteshwar Pujara has stepped up in this home season. But this knock has put him on a different pedestal. He batted for almost 78 overs with Wriddhiman Saha, who also scored a century and gave India a lead of 152 runs. Hadn't it been for Pat Cummins' outstanding bowling where he scalped four wickets, the home side could've scored a lot more.

An outstanding Test match really. It all started with a well deserved century from Steven Smith who remained unbeaten on 178. It was an innings which he will remember for a very long time. Some innings raise the bar of the batsman and this from Smith was one of them. Glenn Maxwell, too, was fantastic in his comeback as he registered his maiden ton. Ravindra Jadeja was the pick of the bowlers for India as he sent five Australian batsmen back to the hut and ended the match with nine wickets.

The improbable has happened. Australia have managed to bat out the whole day and no it wasn't Steven Smith who led from the front. But Shaun Marsh and Peter Handscomb who stitched together a 124-run stand and played 62.1 overs. Kohli and Rahane acknowledge Handscomb's knock and convey the same to him with a handshake and some words. The series is still alive and the decider will be played in Dharamsala!

...DAY 5, SESSION 3...

Oh, the calmness this pair showed after losing their captain was tremendous. Darren Lehmann pointed out yesterday that batting against the old ball would be considerably easy and India struggled with the old cherry. The one chance that they managed to create was put down by Karun Nair at FSL. Minimum 29 overs and six wickets! The tale of the last session would be exhilarating. Join us in a bit to find out what happens.

FOUR! Expensive over. 14 runs off the over. Full and on off, Handscomb charges down the track and clips it extremely well through mid-wicket to score the third boundary of the over.
Tossed up around off, Peter comes down the track and blocks.
FOUR! Runs leaking now. Marginally short and outside off, Handscomb goes back and cuts this through covers for a boundary. 10 off the last four balls.
Marsh tucks this shortish delivery through square leg for one run.
Fuller and on off, Handscomb uses his feet and clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Brilliant use of feet! Flighted delivery, but Peter comes down the track and converts it into a full toss. Flicked away through square leg for a boundary. Australia trail by 31 runs.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up outside off,  Marsh is rock solid in defense.
FOUR! Marsh comes down the track, opens the face of the bat and looks to drive this floated delivery.. However the ball takes the leading edge and rolls away through point for a boundary.
Slides this down around off, Marsh defends it.
Fullish and outside off, blocked towards the off side.
Flatter and quicker on off, defended to FSL.
Bowls the leg spinner, ends as a full toss, Marsh drives it towards mid off and runs one.
50-run stand between Marsh and Handscomb!
Peter gets to the pitch of this fullish delivery and clips it towards mid-wicket. Single taken.
Full and on the sticks, stonewalled.
Floats this one around middle, Marsh clips it towards mid on and runs one.
Tosses this one around off, stays low, Marsh defends it well after getting his willow down in time.
Flighted delivery, Handscomb uses his feet and clips to mid on. One run taken.
Short and outside off, PH goes back and punches it through covers for a single.
Loops this one on off, Handscomb buries it.
Floats this one outside off, drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Similar delivery, same approach.
Tosses this one around middle, PH defense is solid.
Fuller and on the sticks, Handscomb makes room and drives it to covers.
Time for drinks.
Marsh gets to the pitch of this floated delivery and manoeuvres it towards the leg side.
Tossed up delivery, outside off, defended towards silly point.
Loops this one around middle, Marsh offers a front foot defense.
Full and on the sticks, bunted back to the bowler.
Pitched outside leg, Marsh pads it away.
Bowls it slower through the air and around leg, Marsh buries it.
Sticks to the full length, around off, PH sticks to his defense.
Jadeja appeals, no one else does. Quicker and flatter, Peter looks to defend but gets beaten by the turn and Saha collects it. Jaddu thought there was some noise no one else did.
Short and outside off, Handscomb camps back and punches it towards the off side.
Tosses this one outside off, drives it towards the cover fielder.
Fuller and on the sticks, PH defends it right under his eye line.
Full and on off, Handscomb's drive hits the silly point.
Floats this on middle, Marsh blocks it towards the FSL.
Tosses this one around off, Marsh leans to defend.
Full and outside off, Marsh dead-bats it.
Short and around leg, Marsh tucks it to square leg.
Drags his length back and keeps it outside off, flicked towards mid-wicket.
Fuller and on the pads, stonewalls it.
Bowls it slightly slower through the air, Handscomb gets his stride forward and drives it towards the off side.
Floated delivery outside off, pushed to covers.
Goes over the wicket and bowls this on the sticks, dead-bats it.
Fuller and on the sticks, Peter buries it.
Tosses this one outside off, Peter leans and drives to covers.
Sprays it around leg, Handscomb blocks it.
Fullish delivery outside off, Marsh is rock solid in defense.
Full and around off, smothered towards the FSL.
Tosses this one around off, Handscomb uses his feet and flicks it past short mid-wicket for one run.
Full delivery, Handscomb gets to the pitch of the ball and whips it to mid-wicket.
Short and around middle, Marsh tucks it through square leg for a single.
Marsh goes forward and blocks this tossed up delivery.
Change of ends for Ravichandran Ashwin.
Pitched outside leg, Peter pads it away.
Handscomb offers a front foot defense to this full delivery.
Handscomb drives this tossed up delivery down the ground.
Short delivery, PH goes back and taps it towards the off side.
Handscomb has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Huge LBW appeal straightaway, Jadeja looks almost certain but the umpire doesn't. Tosses this one around leg, Handscomb pads it away. It was pitched outside leg, hence turned down.
Ravindra Jadeja is back on.
Short delivery around leg, Marsh gets out of its way.
Fuller delivery and angling in, Marsh blocks it off the front foot.
Length ball outside off, from around the wicket, Marsh leaves it alone.

NOT OUT! A very tentative review from Kohli, no one seemed confident and he took it after a long talk. Umesh bangs this short and around leg, it stays low, Marsh looks to leave it alone but it raps his pads. Kohli has a talk with Saha and Umesh and opts for DRS. It is pitched outside leg and no need to go any further.
India review for an lbw against Shaun Marsh. It is not too confident.
Back of a length delivery again, around off, Peter pats it through point. One run taken.
Short of a length delivery, on leg, Handscomb tucks it uppishly towards mid-wicket.
Marsh has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floats this outside off, Marsh pushes it towards the off side.
Tosses this one on off, knocked back to the bowler.
Short and around middle, Marsh camps back to dead-bat.
Fullish delivery, around off, Marsh blocks it.
Marsh offers a front foot defense to this fuller delivery.
Bouncer around leg, Handscomb sways out of its way but it hits something and goes towards the keeper. India appeal but the umpire is not interested.
Full and outside off, PH dabs it to third man for a couple.
Bangs this short again, Marsh looks to get of its way but it hits his chest and rolls towards fine leg. Leg bye taken.
Length ball, which swings away a bit, Marsh leaves it alone.
Short ball around leg, Marsh allows Saha to collect the ball.
Short of a length delivery, angling in, tucked away to fine leg for a single.
Quicker and flatter, outside off, Saha gathers it.
Pitches this one on the rough, Marsh sees the turn and lets it through.
Fullish delivery, outside off, well blocked.
FOUR! Makes it look so easy! Marsh comes down the track and just places this full delivery down the ground. It beats the mid on fielder and races away for a boundary.
Fuller again and on middle, Marsh blocks it.
Full and on off, Marsh bunts it back to the bowler.
Yorker in the blockhole, 144 kph, Handscomb digs it out towards mid-wicket.
Very full and outside off, Handscomb looks to steer it towards third man but it goes on the bounce to first slip.
Short of a length delivery, around off, Marsh guides it down to third man for a single.
Length ball, fifth stump line, Marsh shoulders his arms.
Fuller and on the sticks, Marsh offers a front foot defense.
Second slip moves to short point.
False shot from Marsh! No need to play at those. Umesh bowls it full and way outside off, Marsh looks to chase and goes for the drive but misses.
Floats this one around leg, Handscomb prods forward to block.
Tosses this one around leg, low bounce, jammed towards FSL.
Drags his length back and keeps it around leg, Peter goes back and blocks it with a straight face of the bat.
Full and on the sticks, Handscomb buries it.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Gives this one a lot of flight, ends up being a full toss as PH charges down the track. He flicks it uppishly but fortunately for him it falls short of the short mid-wicket fielder, Murali Vijay.
Short of a length delivery, outside off, tapped towards point.
FOUR! Fabulous shot! Full and angling in, all Marsh did was get his willow down in time. The ball races through the right of the mid on fielder for a boundary.
Fullish delivery, outside off, Marsh has allowed it through.
Marginally ahead of length and on off, Marsh gets on his back foot and offers a front foot defense.
Fuller again and outside off, Handscomb intentionally plays it past the second slip and runs one.
Fullish delivery on the sticks, stays low, PH camps back to block but it takes the inside edge and goes onto hit the pads. Umesh goes up but realizes that there was an edge.
Tossed up outside off, Handscomb goes forward, opens the face of the bat and places it towards third man. One run taken.
Short of a length, Handscomb tucks it away to backward square leg.
Floats this one outside off, PH lunges to block.
Slower through the air and outside off, Handscomb offers a front foot defense.
Peter drives this floated delivery to mid on.
DROPPED! Tough chance goes down. Tosses this one around leg, Handscomb looks to nudge it away but it goes straight to Karun Nair at FSL who fails to hold onto it.
Good length delivery, outside off, Marsh gets on his toes and gets over the ball to stonewall it.
Shortish delivery again, Marsh goes on his back foot to defend.
Short of a length delivery, chest height, Marsh is rock solid in defense.
Fuller again and slightly outside off, Shaun gets beaten on the outside edge as he looks to block.
Angles in a fuller length ball, which comes back in, Marsh pushes it towards the off side.
On a length and outside off, Marsh thinks of a poke but opts against it after seeing that it was swinging away.
Short which skids in, Marsh camps back and clips it through mid-wicket. Nice looking shot and he gets three for it. The mid-wicket fielder chases it and cuts it off.
Bowls it slower through the air and on middle, Marsh dead-bats it.
In the air...safe! Floats this one around middle, Handscomb looks to defend but it takes the inside edge and goes past the diving leg gully fielder. Single taken.
Full and on the sticks, blocked.
Tosses this one outside off, Handscomb dances down the track and defends.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Ravichandran Ashwin comes into the attack. Change of ends for him. A slip, leg gully and short leg.
Sprays this down the leg side, Marsh looks to tickle it but it hits the thigh pad and rolls towards fine leg. They take two leg byes.
Short delivery, way outside off, Marsh hops and pats it to point.
Back of a length delivery, outside off, guided down to third man for a single.
On a length and sixth stump line, Peter leaves it alone.
Very full and outside off, Handscomb lets it through. Saha gathers it in front of his face.
Starts with a good length delivery, which nips back in, Handscomb goes back to block.

Shaun Marsh and Peter Handscomb walk out in the middle. This pair came to India with good reputation against spin and the time wouldn't get any better than this. They have a chance to portray their credentials. But can they do so? Stay with us to find out.
...DAY 5, SESSION 2...

Ravindra Jadeja was being himself, very accurate! Steven Smith looked confident during his stay at the crease but a rare misjudgement from the Australian captain cost him his wicket and Jadeja's accuracy paid rich dividends. The Australians controlled the first hour but India roared back in the second. Shaun Marsh was very active and looked solid. Can he continue the same in the next session? Only time will tell. Join us in a bit for the post-lunch session.

In Test cricket, everything matters. A change of ball or even an altercation could change the game. That is what happened today. Matt Renshaw pulling out of a delivery when Ishant Sharma was in his bowling stride made the latter angry, and it was enough for the pacer. He steamed in on the fourth ball of that over, trapped his man LBW and exuberant celebrations followed.

Jadeja changes his line and goes very full on off, Handscomb squeezes it out through point and Umesh Yadav gives the chase. He pulls it back before the rope and saves a run for his side. That will be lunch on day 5!
Loopy and landing on the rough outside leg, Peter takes a good stride forward and pads it away.
Pitches it a touch short and down the leg side, Handscomb pads it away.
Slow loopy full ball on off, it's driven confidently off the front foot to mid off.
Tossed up ball on middle, clipped in front of square leg for one.
Flighted full ball on off, defended off the front foot to the off side.
Flatter this time, skidding through from off and staying low, Marsh luckily manages to get his bat down in time and keeps it out to mid-wicket. It's in the gap and they cross for a run.
Charges down to the pitch of the delivery and pushes it to short extra cover.
Drifting in and spinning away outside off, Marsh leaves it alone.
Loopy on off, defended off the front foot.

Huge shout for an lbw! Ashwin bowls a slider around off, Marsh gets forward to defend with his bat coming down late. He is hit on the front pad, they appeal but nothing from the umpire. The point of impact was the issue.
Starts his spell from around the wicket and bowls a tossed up off spinner outside off, Marsh shoulders arms.
Ravichandran Ashwin comes into the attack 4 minutes before lunch.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. No run.
Brilliant delivery, an arm ball bowled on the shorter side around off, not rising much, Peter gets back and somehow keeps it out at the last moment.
Comes from around the wicket and fires in a fuller ball on off, Handscomb gets forward with a big stretch and defends it down.
Spinning back in from around off, Marsh nudges it through backward square leg for one.
Marsh has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Deep square leg goes to deep mid-wicket.
FOUR! Loose delivery and duly punished! Jadeja bowls it a bit short and gets it to spin back in, Marsh goes back hits it firmly through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full and angling in around off, Marsh gets squared up a bit before pushing it with an angled bat to backward point. A single taken.
Fuller and on middle, flicked to deep backward square leg for one.

Four byes! Sharma spears in a full ball but way down the leg side, Peter fails to flick and Saha has no chance of collecting it with a dive to his left. Bonus runs for Australia, they trail by 81 runs.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

No ball called for overstepping! Ishant bowls a full inswinging delivery on off, Marsh leans forward and across to flick it off the inside half of the bat to deep backward square leg. Jadeja makes a sliding stop in the deep and they take a single.
Fullish and angling into the batsman from around off, Marsh presses ahead and defends it back.
Zippy delivery, a touch short and outside off, Shaun stays back and leaves it. Ishant is looking in good rhythm now.
Floated full ball on off, driven firmly off the front foot, with the spin but it came off the outside half of the bat. It hit the silly point fielder low on the left leg. No real chance to react.
Pitching outside leg, Peter once again pads it away.
Loopy full ball on middle, Handscomb defends it off his front foot.
Fires a flatter full ball outside leg, Peter takes a big stride forward and pads it away.
Jadeja loses his grip on the ball and it falls from his hand. Rolls towards the keeper.
Tickles it off his pads to the leg side and takes a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On a length and angling back into the batsman, Marsh gets forward and defends it to the off side towards cover-point. One run added to the total.
A touch short in length and outside off, straightening a bit off the seam, Marsh feels for it and gets beaten.
Back of a length ball drifting down the leg side, once again Marsh shoulders arms and moves away from the line.
Slips one down the leg side, Marsh moves away from the line and leaves it alone.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Hurls in a full length delivery in the channel outside off, Shaun shoulders arms.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. No run.
Another front foot defense by Peter.
Fires it full on off, 90 kph, Handscomb defends it off his front foot.
Gets on the front foot in defense.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Peter Handscomb is the new man in.

OUT! Sound of timber and the crowd erupts. Jadeja is up and running in celebration. He lands a full ball just around leg on the rough. Smith takes his front leg forward a bit and thinks he has covered the spin. But to his disappointment, the ball curls away and goes on to uproot the off stump. The Indian players know the importance of this wicket and are celebrating big time. Smith walks back dejected. The Ranchi crowd has gone bonkers. It's a massive blow to Australia.
Sharp delivery, landing shortish on off and shooting up, Marsh gets across to defend but misses and is hit on the body.
FOUR! In the region outside off, Marsh has a nervous poke inside the line and gets a soft outside edge down to third man for a boundary,
Shaun Marsh has arrived at the crease.

OUT! Renshaw is trapped in front and Ishant is all pumped up. He has won this battle and is mobbed by his teammates. Finally a wicket this morning for India. Smart bowling by Sharma, bowled a couple of short ones and this time hurls in a full length ball on off. Angling in and staying low, Renshaw gets forward to defend but misses and is hit on the front pad. Ishant roars in appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Matt has a chat with his skipper and decides not to take the DRS. The umpire quickly checks for the no ball but Ishant is fine with his landing. The banter seems to have put Renshaw off. Australia trail by 93 runs.
Matt Renshaw is adjudged lbw and he walks back without taking the DRS. The umpire though is checking for the no ball.
Shortish and angling down the leg side, Matt tries flicking but misses.

Back of a length ball angling in, Renshaw fails to keep it out and is hit on the thigh pad. The ball pops out and gets stuck in the grille of the helmet. No harm done. In fact Matt has a smile on his face.
Good length ball angling in, Renshaw defends it from the back foot. Ishant sledges and Renshaw returns the compliment.

Ishant Sharma steams in but Matt Renshaw pulls out as there was some movement near the sightscreen. Sharma frustratingly throws the ball to the keeper. Words exchanged and things getting heated up in the middle. The umpires get involved and have a chat with Kohli and Renshaw.
Fuller and on off, defended back with a straight bat.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it down safely.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Peach of a delivery! Loopy again, landing full around off, Smith lunges to defend but it turns away with extra bounce to beat the outside edge.
Loopy full ball on off, it's defended off the front foot.
Flatter and full on off, Smith defends it watchfully.
Edged but safe! On a length and outside off, Renshaw pushes at it with an angled bat and gets it away off the outer half of the bat. It drops on one bounce to gully.
Very full and around off, Renshaw gets on the front foot and defends it.
Ishant persists with a full length ball outside off, Renshaw covers the line and allows it through to the keeper.
Goes very full this time, outside off, inviting the batsman to have a drive but Renshaw makes a watchful leave.
Length and angling into the batsman, around off and straightening a touch, Matt gets on the front foot in defense.
Too full in length on middle, Smith gets across the stumps and flicks it through backward square leg for a run.
Quicker full ball on off, flicked firmly to mid-wicket where the fielder made a diving stop.
Tossed up ball outside off, Matt lunges to defend, plays for the spin but it goes a bit straight and beats the outside edge.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball and flicks it with the spin to short mid-wicket.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Four byes! Spin and bounce from outside off, Renshaw gets across to defend but misses as it sneaks past him and the keeper to the fine leg fence.
Floated full ball landing outside off, Matt lunges and defends it with his bat and pad together.
On a length and in the channel outside off, SS shoulders arms.
FOUR! Typical Steven Smith wristy shot. Ishant angles in a fuller length ball on middle, the Aussie skipper moves across the stumps and clips it beautifully through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full and wide outside off, shaping away, an easy leave for Smith. Ian Gould shouts no ball for overstepping.
A touch short and on middle, Renshaw gets back and helps it to square leg for one.

This time he goes full and around off, Renshaw gets forward and defends it with an angled bat to gully. Ishant runs straight in the danger area in his followthrough and umpire Ian Gould is quick to have a chat with him.
Good length and on off, Matt gets back and defends it to short mid-wicket.
Ishant steams in from around the wicket and angles in a back of a length ball on off, Renshaw gets behind the line solidly and defends.
Ishant Sharma to continue with a short third man in place.

Time for drinks. The pair of Steven Smith and Matt Renshaw has shown tremendous maturity and has been really solid so far. The plan from India was to dry up the runs from one end, as the pacers bowled way outside off to the Australian captain, and let Jadeja attack from the other end.
A bit of a negative line this. Landing in the rough outside leg, Smith just pads it away.
Loopy and just outside leg, Smith leans forward and defends it with his bat and pad together.
Identical to the last delivery, once again Smith uses his pads to keep it out.
Comes from over the wicket and lands it full outside leg, Smith pads it away.
Flatter and on off, punched down to mid on.
Flighted and full ball on middle, Smith brings down a straight bat in defense.
Switches to around the wicket and angles in a full ball on off, Renshaw gets behind the line and blocks it safely.
A fine gully in place for Matt Renshaw.
Too full in length outside off, Smith drives it straight back and Ishant only manages to make a half stop in his followthrough. The mid off fielder does the mopping up job and they cross for a run.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, Smith allows it through.
Full in length and wide outside off, staying low, Smith gets across the stumps and allows it through.
Fuller in length and outside off, Smith reaches out and strokes it through cover-point for a couple of runs.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Virat Kohli is back on the field. It seems he has gone to attend the nature's call.
Flighted ball landing way outside off, Renshaw tries to defend but it goes underneath his bat. Saha fails to collect it cleanly.
Loopy and landing outside off, breaking back in sharply from the rough, Renshaw tries to defend but misses. It hits him high on the pads.
Flatter and shorter on off, spinning in, Matt goes back in defense.
Gets forward to a full ball and blocks it safely.
Full flighted ball outside off, Renshaw gets forward with a big stride and tries to defend it with soft hands. It comes off the outside edge and runs wide of first slip for a couple of runs.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Virat Kohli is going off the field. Hopefully nothing serious. Abhinav Mukund is the substitute fielder. Ravindra Jadeja to continue with two short leg fielders now.
Pitches it up and just outside off, Smith plays a confident off drive but finds the fielder.

Great placement. Fuller in length and wide outside off, Smith reaches out for it and drives it through backward point. The third man fielder moves across to his right to stop the ball and they take a couple of runs.
Oversteps and bowls a no ball. The line and length, however, remains the same. Wide outside off. Smith has nothing to do with it.
Waste of a delivery and energy. Full and way wide outside off, the batsman is not troubled at all.
Drops it full and outside off, Smith shuffles across the stumps and pushes it square of the wicket on the off side. Straight towards the point fielder.
Another delivery served in the zone outside off, Smith shouldered arms.
A gentle loosener, wide outside off on a fuller length, Smith allows it through.
Ishant Sharma replaces Umesh Yadav.
Spinning back in sharply from outside off, Matt lunges to defend but misses. It brushes his front pad, then takes the inside edge and pops out. But it falls wide of short leg.
Tossed up ball on off, Renshaw is forward in defense. Confident!
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Turning back in from around off, Renshaw moves across the stumps and defends it to the leg side.
Leans forward and pushes it with the spin towards mid on.

Flighted ball landing outside off, Renshaw lunges to get away from the line of the stumps and tries to defend. Fails to do so and is hit on the pads. A stifled appeal for an lbw but nothing from the umpire.
Action replay of the last delivery. Yadav has not made the batsman play enough deliveries and is culprit of bowling too wide outside off.
Full and outside off, Smith makes another leave.
On a length and outside off, another leave from Steven Smith.
Full and just outside off, staying low, Smith covers the line and allows it through to the keeper.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Fullish and outside off, Smith reaches out for it and opens the face of the bat. He guides it fine towards third man and returns for the second run.
Lunges to a full ball and blocks it safely to end a testing over.
Flatter ball on off, defended of the back foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter and shorter landing outside off, spinning in, Renshaw takes his front leg away from the line of the stumps and pads it away.

Once again turning back sharply into the batsman, Renshaw tries to defend by getting across the stumps but misses. It goes off his pads to first slip. Jadeja appeals for an lbw but the impact is outside off.
Uppish but safe! Sharp bounce and spin from the rough outside off, Renshaw gets back to defend but it takes the inside half of the bat and drops in front of leg gully.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Angles in a length ball on off, Renshaw gets across a bit to come behind the line and defends it to the leg side.
On a length and in the region outside off, Renshaw shoulders arms.
Full and angled in from around off, Renshaw gets a shade squared up and pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Good length delivery in the region outside off, Matt allows it through.
Yadav switches to around the wicket for Renshaw and bowls a length ball wide outside off, an easy leave.
Again it's defended solidly by Smith to end the over. Looking unperturbed at the moment.
Quicker and fuller on off, Smith defends it off his front foot.
Loopy and on off, Smith lunges and defends it with his pad and bat together.
Fullish and on off, easily defended off the front foot to the off side.
Flatter arm ball on off, Smith goes back and keeps it out to short mid-wicket.
Floated full ball on off, Smith strides forward and defends it to mid on.
Reaches out for a full ball outside off and pushes it square of the wicket on the off side for a run.

Edged but safe! Yadav draws a false shot this time. He bowls it on a full length outside off, Smith gets across the stumps and has a needless poke at it. The ball hardly bounces and catches a little outside edge. Doesn't carry to the keeper.
Yadav seems to be playing on the patience of Smith. Hurls another full ball wide outside off, the Aussie skipper is content in leaving it.
Pitches it full this time but the line remains wide outside off, Smith has nothing to do with it.
Wayward bowling this by Yadav. Lets out another delivery wide outside off and it's an easy leave for Smith.
Way wide outside off, full in length and holding its line, Smith allows it through to the keeper.
Loopy full ball on off, once again Renshaw uses his long reach and defends it confidently near his front pad.
Bowls it in the flatter trajectory and gets it to break back into the batsman from outside off, Renshaw defends it off his back foot.
Floated full ball on off, Renshaw gets forward with a big stride and drives it to mid off.
Leans forward to a full ball landing in the rough outside off and smothers it on the leg side.
Quicker and flatter outside off, 90 kph, Matt goes on the back foot in defense. Solid, so far.

Tossed up ball landing outside off, Renshaw gets forward to defend but the ball doesn't spin back in enough and takes the outside edge. It runs wide of first slip and short third man and they take a brace.

Oohhh...this one stays low. Umesh lands it on a full length outside off, Smith makes a leave and it hardly bounces. Saha does well to collect it behind the stumps. Maybe, this one hits one of the cracks on the pitch.
Fullish and around off, shaping back in, Smith stays back and defends it to the bowler.
Good length delivery outside off, another leave by the Aussie skipper.
Full and wide outside off, Smith watches the line closely and lets it through to the keeper.
Hurls in another delivery in the channel outside off, holding its line, Smith allows it through.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Edged but safe! Jadeja sends one quicker through the air, around off and Renshaw gets squared up in defense. It takes a little outside edge but doesn't carry to first slip.
Slower through the air, full and on off, Renshaw presses forward and clips it with the spin to short mid-wicket.
Flatter and shorter on off, defended off the back foot.
Renshaw has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Loopy and around leg, Smith walks down and forces it towards wide mid on for a run.
Flighted full ball on off, driven to covers.
Short ball again, Renshaw decides to leave it.
Digs in a short ball on off, Smith pulls it through square leg and takes a single.
Angles in a full ball on off, Smith gets behind the line again and defends it back safely.
Full in length and just outside off, Smith moves across the stumps and defends it from the middle of the bat.
Back of a length ball on middle, Renshaw goes back and turns it off his hips through backward square leg for a run.
Yadav steams in from around the wicket and angles in a length ball on off, Renshaw sticks back and defends it to the off side.
Fuller and on off, Smith gets forward to drive. It goes a bit uppishly but safely to mid off.
Extra bounce from the rough outside off, Renshaw goes back and taps it down to short third man for a run.
Leans forward to a full ball and pushes it back to the bowler.
Full and on off, driven down to mid on.
A touch flatter and landing outside off, not turning much, Renshaw gets back to defend but it whizzes past the outside edge.
Flighted ball on off, Renshaw gets on the front foot and defends it.

FOUR! Beautiful shot! Yadav overpitches a shade and lands it around off, angling in, Smith leans forward and drives it crisply through covers for a cracking boundary. This shot shows that the pitch is still good enough for batting.
Length delivery around off, Smith covers the line and defends it safely.
Goes very full this time on off, Smith gets across the stumps again, his natural trigger movement and drives it nicely to mid on.
On a length and around off, staying low, Smith gets across the stumps, does well to keep his eyes on the ball as he defends it back.
Pitches it full and outside off, Smith pushes it with good timing to the off side but finds the cover fielder.

Full and angling into the batsman, Smith picks it off his pads and flicks it past the square leg umpire. KL Rahul moves swiftly across to his left in the deep and makes the stop. Two runs added to the total.
Umesh Yadav will bowl from the other end. Two slips in place.
Floated ball landing full on off, Renshaw tries to drive through covers but it spins in and takes the inside edge. Rolls safely to mid-wicket.
Arm ball on middle, fired in and skidding down, Smith gets back to flick but misses. The keeper fails to collect and they cross for a bye.
Flighted again but it's too full on off, Smith drives it firmly through the line but straight to mid off.
Tossed up ball on middle, Smith gets forward and defends it back to the bowler.
Time to play the game! Matt Renshaw walks out to the centre with the new batsman Steven Smith. Ravindra Jadeja to continue with his over. Two slips and a silly point in place.

Pitch report - Australia look under pressure after losing two wickets. There's a lot of rough outside the off stump for left-handers, which will be a problem. Even right-handers might have issues given how Nathan Lyon got out. Jadeja and Ashwin both could exploit that region. The pacers should bowl stump to stump as the odd ball is keeping low.

The match is tilted in hosts' favour. It would take an extraordinary effort from the Aussies to survive the day. Steven Smith will need strong support from his batsmen as he alone cannot save the game for his side. The home side have almost been invincible on slow turners during the home season. Will that pattern continue or we are about to see something from the visitors? Stay with us to find out.

Hello and welcome to the coverage of the fifth day of the third Test between India and Australia. A fifth day pitch in India and all the talks are about Ravindra Jadeja and not Ravichandran Ashwin. Such is the rough outside the off stump that experts have declared the former as the danger man. The Australian southpaws would have to adjust very well to him, taking middle and off stump guard could be useful. Just how Indian right-handers (especially Ajinkya Rahane) changed their technique against Nathan Lyon in Bengaluru's second innings.
...DAY 5, SESSION 1...

With 8 overs to negotiate, Australia suffered an early blow when Ravindra Jadeja breached David Warner's defense and shattered his stumps. Their nightwatchman Nathan Lyon was also quickly sent back by Jadeja and a big task awaits the visitors tomorrow. They trail by 129 runs and with the pitch offering ample assistance to the spinners, it will require a monumental effort and plenty of application from the Aussies to come out of this Test unscathed. Promises to be an intriguing last day. Do join us at 0930 local (0400 GMT) for all the action. Cheers!

End of an entertaining day of Test cricket. Day 4 started with the match on a knife-edge and India seized the initiative on the back of a stupendous partnership between Cheteshwar Pujara and Wriddhiman Saha. The pair batted for two sessions and kept the Australians at bay. Courtesy their contribution and a late quickfire knock by Ravindra Jadeja, the hosts managed to gain a 152-run lead.

OUT! Bowled 'em! The nightwatchman departs. Probably it was too much to ask of Lyon to face Jadeja on a track that is spitting venom. Jadeja pitches this around middle, Nathan goes forward to defend but gets beaten by the turn. Out comes the off stump and Jadeja has his finger on the lips again. Just the start India wanted. Smith and Lehmann have a worried look in the dressing room. And that is it on day 4. Stumps!
Lyon defends this flatter delivery on the off side.
Bowls it on the sticks, Renshaw dead-bats it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter delivery, Renshaw clips it towards the leg side.
Bowls it slower through the air and on off, Matt blocks it.

FOUR! Floats this one around off, Renshaw flicks it through mid-wicket. Pujara gives it a long chase and tries to pull it back just before the rope. But the replays show that his boots were in contact with the fence when he was in contact with the ball. First boundary for Matt Renshaw.
Tosses this one around off, Renshaw blocks it.
Lyon has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Lyon looks to defend but it goes off his inside edge past short leg. Two runs added to the total.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
LBW Appeal. Turned down. Tossed up around middle, Lyon looks to defend but it hits his pads. India go up but the umpire is not interested. It was going down the leg side.
Lyon defends this tossed up delivery towards square leg.
Nathan Lyon is the nightwatchman.

OUT! Cleaned him up. Quicker delivery which turns back in viciously after landing on the rough outside off and Warner is beaten all ends up. The ball doesn't disturb the bails but absolutely crashes the stumps as Warner looks to defend by crouching. The off stump is pegged back and the celebrations are ballistic. Kohli knows how the Australians mocked him and pats his shoulder to probably say who is the boss! Scenes all around. Steven Smith is flabbergasted in the dressing room and wants to look at the replays. David Warner walks off, yet another failure for him.
Shorter again and outside off, Renshaw rocks back to block.
Loops this one around off, Renshaw dead-bats it.
Short and on the sticks, Renshaw goes back to block.
Fuller and on the stumps, whipped away to mid-wicket.
Tosses this one outside off, Warner drives it through mid off for a single.
Warner lunges and blocks this floated delivery.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball as it skids past the outside edge.
Bowls it outside off, Renshaw looks to poke but gets beaten.
Renshaw looks to defend but it goes off his thigh pad towards the FSL.
Tossed up delivery, around off, Matt has blocked it.
Renshaw prods forward and defends this floated delivery on the front foot.
Tosses this one around off, Renshaw looks to defend but it takes the inside edge and goes past towards the leg gully.
Tosses this one outside off, Warner goes back and punches to covers.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

India go up for an LBW! But the umpire is unmoved. Fuller and on the sticks, Warner looks to block but misses and it hits the pad. Ashwin is ecstatic and appeals instantly. But the umpire turns it down. Replays showed that it was quite close.
Warner drives this floated delivery towards mid off.
FOUR! Warner is looking to attack. Tosses this one around middle, David charges down the track and chips it over mid off for a boundary. The shot wasn't convincing but he gets his reward nonetheless.
Full and on the sticks, David's front foot defense goes off the inside edge, hits his pads and lobs towards the off side.
Short again, he is looking to bowl in the rough, Renshaw knocks it back towards the bowler.
Short again, Renshaw rocks back and works it around in front of square for a brace.
Shorter delivery, spins back in, David nudges it towards deep square leg. One run taken.
Shortish and spinning in, Renshaw tucks it through square leg. Single taken.
Gives this a lot more flight, Renshaw looks to defend but it goes off the outside edge towards point.
Faster and flatter, around off Renshaw blocks it.
Ravindra Jadeja will bowl from the other end.
FOUR! Poor bowling from Ash. Bowls it wide again, Warner camps back and cuts it through point for another boundary. Eight runs off the first over.
Shortish again and outside off, dabbed away to point.
FOUR! Short and wide, Warner gets on his back foot and slashes it through covers for a boundary. Gets off the mark with that shot.
Appeal! Turned down. Ashwin tosses this one around off, David looks to defend but it goes off the inside edge onto the pads. The reason why the umpire turned it down.
Gives this one a lot of flight and keeps it outside off, cut to point.
Starts the over with a tossed up delivery on the sticks, Warner makes room and drives it to the cover fielder.
